Founded the Vinnie Keane West Oakland Baseball Academy in a rehabbed Mandela Parkway firehouse — free baseball at all levels. Born 2003, Boston. CitizenBio: Born 1999, Oakland. Former Oakland Police Department public information officer who crossed over to journalism; the rank rides along as an earned credential, not a current commission, and the Tribune keeps it on her byline because it is the whole reason readers trust the copy. Covers crime, safety events and the OPD interface from Uptown. Writes incident analysis rather than incident reports — pursuit protocols, dispatch categories, what "no report filed" actually means — and interviews officers by name, age and years of service. Finds the story in the gap between what happened and how it got categorized. Masters degree, divorced, no children. A quarter-century across the two careers; last promoted C98. Her net worth outruns her Tribune salary several times over: the police years are still on the books.

CitizenBio: Born 1984, Oakland. Sabermetrics man who used to run a minor-league data blog, then spent years as Anthony Raines' statistical support — the name in the footnote of somebody else's column. Promoted C102 to the Tribune's citywide Data Desk, the paper's retrieval and verification seat across every beat: forty years of cleaning other people's numbers and, until that cycle, never once a byline of his own. Registered tone is factual and monotone, which he does not apologise for; accuracy is the contribution. Lives alone on Piedmont Ave, no children, walks home through the neighborhood instead of driving. A connector by temperament — talks with strangers long enough to learn a name. Carries more net worth than his Tribune salary explains, from the years before the paper.

CitizenBio:
Jax Caldera is thirty-eight years old and technically homeless. He lists his address as Longfellow but he's been couch-surfing from Jingletown to Bushrod for two years. He got blacklisted from every alt-weekly in the Bay for being, in his words, "too mean to sacred cows." Now he only writes when he smells blood in the water.

He has no desk at the Tribune. Mags calls him when she needs someone to ask the question nobody else will ask. He shows up, files one piece, and disappears. His pieces are short, hot, and uncomfortable. He doesn't do follow-ups. He lights the match and walks away.

He has a master's degree in urban planning from Berkeley. He doesn't mention it. He'd rather you think he's just some loudmouth at a bar. The precision in his questions gives him away if you're paying attention.
